label: Step 3 input u/0/d/f after a specific k/y-led 3-token prefix
explanation: Fires almost only at step t == 3 (99.7% of mass): usually the 4th original token, or the <DEL> step when L = 3 (~4.5% of mass). It does NOT fire at any other step or anywhere in the copy phase. At t = 3 the input token matters: u > 0 > d > f > h (u/0/d/f carry ~90% of mass); other tokens almost never fire it. On top of that the 3-token prefix gates it additively: first token k or y (k strongest), second token k/1/n/y/t, third token 1/x/t/z/l/s. The top activations are sequences like k 1 t [u], y t x [u], k n 1 [d]. Having all three prefix positions favorable gives about 86% precision but only about 21% recall; requiring 2 of 3 trades precision (~0.30) for recall (~0.72, mass ~0.83). Magnitude is highest when the input is u and the first token is k or y. It looks like a fine-grained conjunctive (lookup-table-like) detector of step-3 context, not a clean concept.
